description:
About the Position

Lund University advertises a doctoral position in medical radiation physics focused on tritium persistence in soils and sediments. Tritium - a radioactive isotope of hydrogen released by nuclear facilities - behaves in environmental systems in ways that are still imperfectly understood, and the project studies how organically bound tritium persists in soils and sediments, how it moves through food chains, and what this means for radiological assessment. The doctoral position is a salaried employment under the Swedish collective agreement, based in Lund's medical radiation physics environment.

Medical radiation physics at Lund combines hospital-linked medical physics with environmental and radiological research, offering laboratory analysis, field sampling and radioanalytical measurement as core methods. The doctoral candidate will design sampling campaigns, run radioanalytical measurements and interpret results in collaboration with radiation-safety and environmental researchers, contributing to both scientific publications and assessment practice relevant to Swedish regulators.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in physics, medical physics, radiochemistry, environmental science or a related quantitative discipline, with an interest in radioactivity and environmental measurement. Laboratory experience and careful analytical practice are valued. Applications are submitted through Lund University's Varbi portal with CV, transcripts and references; the closing date should be confirmed on the official vacancy page.

Highlights

  • PhD in medical radiation physics - tritium persistence
  • Soils, sediments and food-chain pathways
  • Radioanalytical measurement and field sampling
  • Hospital-linked research environment in Lund
  • Salaried employment per Swedish collective agreement
  • Closing date - confirm on the official vacancy page
